# v1.3.0-487: Recognising any app's windows, and merging on Re-capture

Builds on `v1.3.0-479`. That release recognised windows by what they show
for a handful of IDEs. This one does it for any app, using what Windows
itself knows about a window, and lets a Re-capture keep the windows you
don't have open right now.

## Recognising windows

- Any app that runs one window per process is recognised by the file or
  folder it has open, taken from what the app tells Windows about how to
  restart it, or else from how it was started. Two Paint windows, two
  Visual Studio solutions or two copies of a text editor no longer swap
  places when their titles change.
- File Explorer windows are recognised by the folder they show, even
  though every one of them runs in the same process. A window you've
  since navigated somewhere else isn't ruled out, just not preferred.
- Packaged apps such as Windows Terminal, Notepad and anything from the
  Store now carry their app ID.
- VS Code forks (Cursor, VSCodium, Insiders) and every JetBrains IDE
  (IntelliJ, PyCharm, WebStorm and the rest, not only Rider) are
  recognised by their open folder or project. WLM finds them from what
  their install says, not from the program's name.
- A floating panel of any app whose title only repeats its main window's
  is told apart by the name Windows accessibility gives it.
- Hovering a window in the list shows what it's recognised by: its
  document, panel, app ID and desktop.

## Re-capture

- The Re-capture dialog has a new option, "Keep saved windows that
  aren't open now". With it ticked, windows that are open take their new
  places, new ones are added, and saved windows you don't have open keep
  their entries, edits and all. Unticked, Re-capture replaces the saved
  windows as before. Your last choice is remembered.

## Also

- In the list view, the window card opens when you hover the app and
  title, not anywhere on the row.

## Good to know

- Save or Re-capture a profile once to record the new details. Existing
  profiles load exactly as before until then.
- Two windows of one process that show no document, such as two Chrome
  windows on the same profile, still have nothing in Windows that tells
  them apart. Their position and desktop decide, as before.
- A capture with File Explorer, Visual Studio or a quiet floating panel
  open takes around half a second longer.
